title: DBSR: An Efficient Storage Format for Vectorizing Sparse Triangular Solvers on Structured Grids
problem: Commonly used sparse matrix storage formats for structured grid methods do not efficiently support Sparse Triangular Solver (SPTRSV) operations in utilizing SIMD instruction parallelism on modern multi-core CPUs. Existing formats prevent efficient vectorization and hinder contiguous memory access patterns required for optimal CPU performance.
motivation: SPTRSV is critical for solving structured grid problems in HPC applications, and enabling efficient SIMD utilization can significantly improve computational performance and resource efficiency.
method: DBSR proposes a novel sparse matrix storage format designed specifically for vectorized SPTRSV on multi-core CPUs. The format reorganizes data to enable contiguous memory access and SIMD-friendly computation patterns while optimizing memory footprint. It is evaluated within multigrid solvers and zero fill-in incomplete LU preconditioners, demonstrating effectiveness across ARMv8 and x86 architectures.
key_novelty: A specialized sparse storage format (DBSR) that enables efficient SIMD vectorization of sparse triangular solvers by optimizing data layout for CPU vector instructions and cache locality.
contributions: DBSR sparse storage format enabling SIMD vectorization of sparse triangular solvers
Integration with multigrid algorithms and ILU preconditioners

Consistent performance improvements over mainstream sparse matrix formats
